finding.title: Device answer on one step lets another planned write land during live code with no hold, no record and no review
finding.scenario: A workstation-approved Mission M1 is running code (a live terminal run or shell session, present in bus.liveCode). A second workstation-created Mission M2 (workstation envelope, not started by a device) has step S1 = filesystem.read of a file, answered by the workstation with ask_every_time, and step S2 = filesystem.write of planned content, dependsOn S1. A paired device answers S1 with allow_once. deviceRequestRefusal(S1) passes because deviceResumeRefusal(M2) only inspects M2's own plan (no shell sessions, no terminal, no git, no EXECUTE). S1 runs under the device's one-time allowance, the mission resumes, and S2's filesystem.write runs automatically. remoteActorFor(S2) returns null because M2 is not deviceDriven and S2 has no device-resolved request, so remoteMutationHeld(S2) returns null, the bus records no remote_changes row (bus.server.ts:307 records only when remoteActorFor is truthy), and pendingRemoteReview() stays empty. Result: a device-timed project change lands while workstation code runs and is never listed for review. Content is planned text, but planner.server.ts:191-193 allows a write's content to come from a verified model step's text, and the plan UI (src/components/island/mission.tsx:112) shows only the action name, so that content may never have been displayed to the workstation.
finding.evidence: Reproduced with a throwaway in-process probe (own temp folder, deleted afterwards; no repo writes). Output: 'device answer accepted: true', 'planned.txt written while live code present: planned', 'remote_changes pending (review gate input): 0', 'review listing for next code run: null', 'held? null'. The live-code state was simulated by setting missions.bus.liveCode, which is the same map liveCodeExecutions() reads. Code paths: manager.server.ts remoteActorFor (2318-2330, step-scoped answered check, no check for mission-level answers that resumed the mission), remoteMutationHeld (2389-2400), deviceResumeRefusal (2223, Mission-local only); bus.server.ts:165 and :307. The existing remote-authority test suite (69/69 pass) does not cover a device answer resuming a different planned write during live code.
finding.recommendation: Attribute every mutation that runs after a device answer or device resume in the same Mission, not only the answered step. For example, mark the Mission deviceDriven (markDeviceDriven) when a device answers any of its asks, or record remote_changes for every MUTATIONS run while mission.deviceDriven is set. Also make deviceResumeRefusal (or the hold) consider workstation-approved code that is live anywhere on the Host, not only this Mission's plan. Add a regression test that drives: device answers a read step, a planned write follows, a live-code entry exists, and the write must be held or recorded and listed by pendingRemoteReview().

finding.title: Device revocation leaves workstation Missions and Agents that the device started or resumed running
finding.scenario: A workstation-approved Mission (envelope grantedBy 'workstation') has a planned in-envelope write step that runs without asking. Paired device P calls mission.start; deviceStartRefusal only blocks code, so it is accepted and markDeviceDriven sets deviceDriven=P (manager.server.ts:2353). The workstation revokes P. endDeviceGrants skips any envelope whose grantedBy is not P (line 855), never stops the Mission, and never looks at deviceDriven, so the remaining non-asking steps keep running after revocation. The same applies to an Agent P resumed through agent.resume, because its consent provenance is the workstation's. Code steps still ask the workstation, so this is persistence of a lost device's start/resume rather than device-initiated code execution.
finding.evidence: http.server.ts:855 filters on envelope.grantedBy === deviceActor only; deviceDriven is read only by remoteActorFor (manager.server.ts:2323) and written only by markDeviceDriven (manager.server.ts:2353); no revocation path consumes it. Code-verified; not probed end-to-end because endDeviceGrants is a closure inside startHost.
finding.recommendation: In endDeviceGrants, also stop active Missions whose deviceDriven equals the revoked device, and revoke or pause Agents whose most recent resume came from that device (persist a resumedBy field). Add a regression test that starts a workstation Mission from a device, revokes it, and asserts the Mission stops.

finding.title: Review listing prints file names unescaped, so a file name can fake a prompt entry
finding.scenario: A paired device writes a data file whose name contains U+2028 and U+2022 (NTFS allows both; the write succeeded in the probe). pendingRemoteReview() interpolates the raw path into `\n• ${path}: ...`, so the prompt shows a line break and an extra bullet before the real entry. Only the file content goes through JSON escaping (describeRemoteChange). The round-10 (H) claim that bullets and bidi characters are escaped so text cannot imitate prompt entries holds for content but not for paths. The real entry and its sha256 still follow, so this is a presentation spoof of the review prompt rather than an authority bypass.
finding.evidence: Probe (own mkdtemp folder, deleted): pendingRemoteReview().listing contained raw U+2028 and U+2022 (`RAW U+2028 in listing: true RAW U+2022 in listing: true`). Relevant text: JSON(listing) = "\n• C:\\...\\project\\notes • Calculator check - all clear.txt: 7 bytes, sha256 ...". The same unescaped path also appears in the held-reason text (manager.server.ts:2400) and in deviceChanges (manager.server.ts ~3483).
finding.recommendation: Apply the same escaper used for content (JSON encoding, or explicit escaping of U+2028/U+2029, U+2022, bidi controls and C0 controls) to every path printed in review listings, held-reason text and the deviceChanges reason.

Only describeRemoteChange's content text is JSON-escaped (line 81), so the path is not escaped. A probe confirmed Windows NTFS accepts U+2028 and U+2022 in a file name (bytes e2 80 a8 and e2 80 a2 were written to the filename in a mkdtemp folder, then deleted). The same raw path is also interpolated into the held-reason text (around line 2400) and the deviceChanges reason (line 3482). The impact is presentation-only. Acknowledgment is id-based (ids come from pending.filter over the shown paths, line 2347), not parsed from text, so a fake entry cannot acknowledge anything the workstation did not see, and the real entries with their real SHA-256 and TOO-LARGE flags still follow. The content regex also omits U+200E, U+200F and U+061C. This contradicts the round-10 (H) claim that review previews cannot be imitated, so it is a correctness gap in the stated guarantee, not an authority bypass. LOW is the right severity.

The finding contradicts the round-10 (H) claim that review previews are escaped against prompt imitation, which is a correctness gap in that claim, so it stays reportable at LOW. Not an owner-policy disposition or accepted limitation.

finding.title: Agent pending asks expose the full review listing to paired devices
finding.scenario: A pending review ask on an Agent-owned Mission carries the full listing in its reason: paths, sha256 and up to 8 KB of JSON-encoded content per changed file. projection() copies that reason verbatim into authorization.pending[].reason. The device /state path (http.server.ts viewFor, about lines 352-366) only adds a `remote` verdict to those pending items, dashboardSnapshot (presentation.ts:422) does not touch agents, and remoteVerdicts strips listings only from mission.requests. A paired device can therefore read the content of files that other paired devices changed. This is information disclosure only and grants no execution.

finding.recommendation: In viewFor (device branch), replace pending[].reason with the generic review reason whenever the request has remoteReview or the listing pattern, the same way remoteVerdicts treats mission.requests.

finding.title: Held-ask reason reaches devices with a Host absolute path that the device redaction does not match

The ask reason reads `...a paired-device filesystem.write of C:\Users\...\a.txt waits until it ends...` and names live process labels. remoteVerdicts (about line 2168) replaces the reason only when remoteReview is set. deviceMissionData's regex (line 2238: /changed under paired-device authority|paired-device change/) does not match the held wording. A paired device therefore sees the absolute Host path and live-process labels in /state and mission.get requests, contrary to the stated rule that local folder paths never reach a paired device.

finding.title: Paired devices read the Host-wide review listing (file content) via /state inbox and mission.get memory

finding.evidence: Probe run in a self-created mkdtemp folder under OS temp, importing repo modules by file URL, folder deleted afterwards. finding.recommendation: Apply the device projection to every surface that carries reason text: strip or replace the listing in inbox detail (where the mission.permission_required event is classified), in memory value entries, and in mission.get memory (filter in deviceMissionData). finding.title: Device-chosen file names reach the review prompt unescaped (bidi and line-separator characters)
finding.scenario: describeRemoteChange JSON-escapes file text, but the listing prints each path raw (line 2346: `\n• ${path}: ...`), and the desktop reason prints the raw change paths (line 3482). Windows permits U+2028, U+202E and U+2022 in file names, and filesystem.write accepts such a path (scopedPath only canonicalizes it). A device can name a file 'notes<U+2028><U+202E>evil<U+2022> x.txt'. The workstation prompt then shows those characters raw, so the label can be visually reordered or split, contrary to the stated guarantee that changed-file text cannot imitate prompt entries. The sha256, size and escaped content are still shown, so the impact is a misleading label, not a bypass.
finding.evidence: Probe: a terminal.exec review reason over such a file contained 4 raw U+2028/U+202E/U+2022 characters (one from the path and one from the path's bullet, plus the listing bullet). No escaping was applied to the path.
finding.recommendation: Escape path labels with the same escaping used for content (JSON plus bidi and line-separator escapes), or reject control, bidi and line-separator characters in filesystem.write paths.
